strengths: A death the GMs keep is a row and nothing on the actor: no flag, no status, no bullet deleted until the discovery or a GM's hand, and a row whose save failed falls back to a public death rather than a lost one (death.mjs:165-175, 458-489, persisted() read back at 483).
One function writes what deceased means (markDeceased, death.mjs:67-125), with the body tile and the dead watch each tried on their own so a failure in either keeps the death (107-122).

The discovery is the primary GM's alone and queued on one promise, so a teleport's burst of updateToken announces one body once (body.mjs:125-163, 165-181); its stamp is written before the gather and the card (294-295), and only a published death is named (272-284, 443-452).
Who walked in is decided from reads taken in one synchronous step off the primary's mark (body.mjs:737-809), witnesses counted as students not tokens (680-700).
The witnesses' discovery waits for the GM's word and survives a reload or a GM leaving (pendingBodyStore, body.mjs:840-856, 951-963), with 'Not yet' the default under Enter (937-939).

The End of chapter is one ordered list with a record: a step done is not run again, the clock and the morning move to the ending's own targets (endMoves, chapter.mjs:574-581), the phase is re-read before every step (953-969), and a stopped end is finished or dropped from the window (1009-1077).

The season reset writes its cut before any step and nothing when the cut fails (season-wipe.mjs:806-812), asks primacy again after the typed word and before every step (343-354, 888), and keeps a record that opens the next window on what it left, only while the clock stands where it left it (unfinishedGroups, 748-755).

The registry of season state refuses a second entry, an unknown group and an entry that clears nothing, at load (season-reset.mjs:76-104), and lifetimeProblems holds the world settings' lifetimes to it (147-169).
The day summary reads only the facts this browser was sent (secretSummaries, day-summary.mjs:166-182) and shows nothing on a browser whose clock is hidden for an incident (85-99).

The death fade is DOM only, writes nothing, and goes to its end state at once under reduced motion, the table's switch off, a correction or Escape (death-fade.mjs:278-299); its rest-state write touches only a class the body carries (154-170).
Two GMs making one watcher are settled to one on the primary, by the smallest id, the same answer on every browser (spectator-dead.mjs:381-439).
A Spectator's own moment travels with no student id in the token options (spectator-dead.mjs:25-33, 450-461).

findings.title: Reset the season, Season setup's only door to the reset, closes the window and never opens the reset
findings.what_happens: The frame's button sets resetAsked and calls dialog.close(). drpgWindow is called with rejectClose: false, so the closed window answers null; line 1214 returns null on !result before line 1215 reads resetAsked. End the chapter, wired the same way beside it, works only because its flag is read before the null test (1213). season-wipe.mjs resetSeason is reached from nowhere else in the interface since E101 moved it out of the footer.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM at a season's end opens Season setup and presses Reset the season: the window closes and nothing else happens, so the season cannot be reset from the interface.
findings.expected: The press opens the reset's own typed-word window (season-wipe.mjs resetSeason), as season-setup.mjs:1294-1299 says.
findings.refutation_tried: Read the order of the three tests after the window (1213-1215) and the close: no other answer reaches result when the window is closed by dialog.close(). Searched for another door to resetSeason in scripts/ outside tests: none found besides 1215. This is the same defect as controls-10-setup-config-1, found independently on the domain read; that file's refutation (ui-kit.mjs:1344, R4055's text match) agrees.
findings.tests_near: R4055 and the tier 1 test at scripts/tests-tier1.mjs:20694 match the source line by regular expression and press nothing; result not read (no base-run.json).

findings.title: The death window's 'keep it for the GMs' box is ticked for the incident's victim and stays ticked when the GM picks someone else
findings.where: scripts/death.mjs:736-745 (the default, computed once), 761-763 (the box), 773 and 787 (its answer handed to killCharacter)
findings.what_happens: During an incident the window opens with the victim chosen and the secret box ticked (secretByDefault). Nothing listens to the select: chooseFirst (795-803) only enables the button. A GM who chooses another student keeps the tick, and killCharacter(secret: true) keeps that student's death as a GMs' row: no flag, no marker, their Truth Bullets kept, known only to their owners (incidentKnowers answers [] for anyone but the victim, incident-store.mjs:1225-1230), while the card names the death to the incident's audience as 'kept until found' (death.mjs:283-297).
findings.failure_scenario: Mid-incident a GM opens A character dies to carry out Monokuma's punishment on a bystander, switches the select from the victim to the bystander and confirms: the bystander's death is hidden from the table until somebody walks in on the body, which the GM did not mean.
findings.expected: The box follows the student chosen: ticked for the running incident's victim, the kill's own default (killCharacter: secret ?? isIncidentVictim, death.mjs:176), unticked for anyone else unless the GM ticks it.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a change listener on the select or the box in the window's render (779: chooseFirst alone) and in ui-kit's drpgWindow use here: none. Checked that a non-victim's kept death is reachable: killCharacter takes secret from the answer (787) before its own default (176). The label (DRPG.Chapter.keepSecretUntilFound) is visible beside the select, so the GM can see the tick: hence minor, not major. No test found that changes the select with the box drawn ticked (searched tests-tier2 for keepSecretUntilFound: not searched exhaustively).

findings.title: Split evenly divides the dead too, so the pools it makes can read 'uneven' on the season checklist at once
findings.where: scripts/assignments.mjs:131-156 (autoAssign over students(), dead included); scripts/season-setup.mjs:717-735 (the row counts the living only); scripts/gm-team-dialog.mjs:349-352 (the button's toast)
findings.what_happens: autoAssign deals every student in name order, alternating pools, the dead and the Monocubs included (students() is studentActors() sorted, assignments.mjs:54-56). The despairSplit row counts living students per pool and leaves the dead out (season-setup.mjs:721), and its rule is 'Pools may differ by at most one living student'. A split made mid-season, after deaths, can give one pool two living students more than the other; the button says 'Students split evenly between Monokumas.' and the checklist says 'The pools are uneven'.
findings.failure_scenario: In chapter 3, with two of eight students dead and both in the first pool's alternate seats, a GM presses Split evenly in Despair Flow: one Monokuma watches two living students and the other four, and the Season checklist warns of an uneven split right after the toast said it was even.
findings.expected: Split evenly deals the living (the despairSplit row's own measure, season-setup.mjs:409-423 and S-4), and gives the dead a pool afterwards or leaves them where they were.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether students() leaves the dead out: it is studentActors() sorted, which filters Monokumas, NPCs and Spectators only (monokuma.mjs:77-84). Checked whether the dead matter to a pool: the row's own comment says they do not roll (season-setup.mjs:721). Found no test that splits with a dead student (not searched exhaustively). Severity minor: Despair still flows, only the GMs' share of living students is off.

findings.title: The season reset makes a Spectator for every Monocub and takes it away again in the same step, the churn A113-C2-4 closed for the Students window
findings.where: scripts/season-wipe.mjs:453-458 (wipeStudent's deaths part); scripts/monocub.mjs:207-211 (`watcher: false` and why); scripts/death.mjs:683-692 (clearSeasonDeaths runs removeAllDeadSpectators before the students)
findings.what_happens: For a Monocub the reset's deaths part calls setMonocub(actor, false, { quiet: true }) with no `watcher: false`, so monocubBecomesWatcher makes a new watcher actor (the old ones were already removed by removeAllDeadSpectators) and re-links the Monocub's walking token to it with the moment 'spectator'; the next line's reviveCharacter then deletes that token with 'return' and the actor. monocub.mjs's own note names this: 'a token come and gone on every browser and the player's curtain bare, then lit'. gm-students.mjs:645-650 passes `watcher: false` for the same sequence; the reset does not.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM resets a season with two Monocubs: each Monocub's player sees the curtain go bare and light again, and every browser sees an actor and a token made and deleted, for nothing the reset keeps.
findings.expected: The reset passes `watcher: false` as the Students window does (gm-students.mjs:645-650), since the revive follows.
findings.refutation_tried: Read setMonocub's branch (monocub.mjs:205-212): with watcher defaulting true and the student deceased, monocubBecomesWatcher runs. Read monocubBecomesWatcher (spectator-dead.mjs:326-359): with cub tokens present it makes a watcher by ensureWatcherActorOnly (none exists after removeAllDeadSpectators, death.mjs:688) and re-links the tokens. Read reviveCharacter (death.mjs:619-628) and removeDeadSpectator (233-260): the watcher is found by its watcherOf flag and its tokens and actor deleted. The tier 2 test for A113-C2-4 (tests-tier2.mjs:19021) drives the Students window, not wipeStudent. Nit: the end state is right.

findings.title: A discovery reached while the GM's 'Students found a body' prompt stands is never asked by the prompt
findings.where: scripts/body.mjs:906-913 (one prompt at a time), 915-949 (the rows read once at its start), 849-855 (a walk into a room already waiting does not ask again)
findings.what_happens: promptPendingBodies reads the waiting rows once (917) and asks them in turn; a second room whose witnesses reach the count meanwhile writes its row and calls askPendingBodies, which hands back the running promise (908). When that prompt ends nothing reads the rows again, and further walks into the second room return before asking (850-851). The row is asked again only at the next trigger: another room reaching the count, a reload or GM store hydration, or a GM leaving (956-963). The GM panel's Next line names only the oldest waiting row (gm-panel.mjs:949).
findings.failure_scenario: Two students find one body while the GM still has the prompt for another room open; the GM answers Not yet to the first, and the second discovery is never offered by a prompt - its witnesses were told privately and the table waits until the GM opens Body found.
findings.expected: The prompt reads the waiting rows again after its last answer (or each turn), so every row written while it stood is asked (the owner's decision A of 13.11.2026, body.mjs:840-846).
findings.refutation_tried: Searched for other callers of askPendingBodies: body.mjs alone (855, 957-962) and the facade's re-export (chapter.mjs:56). Checked the Body found window: it names every waiting row in its note (body.mjs:1180-1182), so the GM can still announce it by hand, and the GM panel's Next line shows the oldest (gm-panel.mjs:947-950): hence nit. No test drives two pending rooms with a prompt open (not searched exhaustively).

findings.title: Body found's 'Whose body?' offers a Monocub, unmarked, though no walk-in ever names one
findings.where: scripts/body.mjs:1164-1172 (the list: every student dead for the GMs); 771-778 and 654-668 (the walk-in's rule leaves a Monocub out, BODY-2)
findings.what_happens: The GM's list is studentActors().filter(isDeadForGm): a Monocub keeps the deceased flag, so it is offered as a body beside the dead of every earlier chapter, marked only when this chapter announced it. Named, runDiscovery announces it (the named victim is in victims whatever bodiesToDiscover says, 399-401, 279), stamps it as found and posts 'the body of X' while X walks the map as a Monocub.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM announcing a second murder picks from a list that holds a Monocub of chapter 1 between two names; picking it posts a public card announcing the Monocub's body.
findings.expected: The list leaves out Monocubs (or marks them), by the rule the walk-in reads (bodiesToDiscover).
findings.refutation_tried: Checked runDiscovery for a Monocub guard on the named victim (209-300): only the Eclipse and 'announced already' refuse. Checked whether isDeadForGm is false for a Monocub: it reads the flag and the row only (settings.mjs:3817-3850). The GM chooses the name, so the trap needs a mis-pick: nit.

findings.title: The bare-glass rest state counts an NPC character the player owns as a student, so a dead student's player who also owns one keeps the lit curtain
findings.where: scripts/death-fade.mjs:115-125 (restsBare); scripts/monokuma.mjs:77-84 (studentActors leaves out FLAGS.notInClass too)
findings.what_happens: restsBare walks the player's owned characters and skips Monokumas and Spectators only; a character marked 'Not in the class' (an NPC the player was given) counts as a living student, so restsBare answers false and the curtain never rests bare while that student is dead. Every other roster of students in the module leaves the NPC out (studentActors, studentCensus).
findings.failure_scenario: A player who also runs a shopkeeper NPC the GM gave them dies in an incident: the fade plays and the glass lights again at its rest step after a reload or the next settle, not bare as for every other dead student.
findings.expected: restsBare reads the one roster's rule (FLAGS.notInClass left out), or says why an NPC keeps the curtain lit.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked the fade itself: playCurtain('fade') ends in setRest(true) at 3600 ms (death-fade.mjs:76-77, 244), so the bare state is reached once; it is the settle on a reload (305) and on drpgDeathsChanged/updateActor (334-339) that reads restsBare and lights it again. A player owning an NPC is rare (classCandidates names NPCs as characters no player owns, monokuma.mjs:266-269): nit.

findings.title: Check rooms checks the scene on screen while its row judges the school, and files the result under the screen's scene
findings.where: scripts/season-setup.mjs:1016-1038 (wireRoomCheck: checkRegions() of canvas.scene, lastRoomChecks keyed by canvas.scene.id); 268-277 and 520-521 (the rooms row judges the viewed scene only when it is a place scene, else homeScene, and says which)
findings.what_happens: With the GM looking at a scene that holds no room (the trial hall, a side map), the rooms row reads 'This row checks School' and judges the school, while the row's own Check rooms button runs checkRegions() on the scene on screen, prints that scene's findings under the row and records them under that scene's id, so the row's mark does not move.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM in the trial hall opens the Season checklist, presses Check rooms under 'This row checks School' and reads the hall's findings as the school's.
findings.expected: Check rooms checks the scene the row judges (roomScene), or the row names the scene the button checks.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked checkRegions' default: fog-diagnostics.mjs:547 takes canvas?.scene. Checked workingScene: the viewed scene, else the active one (utils.mjs:611-613), so a viewed hall is no place scene and the row falls to homeScene. Nit: the findings list names its scene's regions, and a GM usually checks from the map being drawn.

l1.what: Whether the discovery sound plays after the Class Trial's end for an executed student's token left on the school map
recipe: Run a chapter to a verdict that executes a student whose token stands in a school room.
As a player who did not stand in that room at the trial, walk a token into it.
